raw_response.blind_rationale:
Blind reading of Zhou & Liang (2021) indicates that this study belongs in `none_nonfit` (with a clear conceptual link to Family A on legal residency recognition that fails on construct and unit/outcome alignment, warranting scope flags on both narrow Criterion 2 and Criterion 4):

1. Exposure / Narrow Criterion 2 (`borderline_governance_or_proxy`): Conceptually, the study frames inequality through China's household registration (`hukou`) legal institution, under which residents lacking local permanent `hukou` are excluded from municipal public-service obligations and urban planning accountability. Empirically, however, the study deliberately restricts its panel to 2008–2014 to avoid the 2014 national `hukou` policy reform and does not measure city-level variation in `hukou` rules, eligibility thresholds, or legal entitlements. Instead, the tested independent variable is the ecological demographic share of temporary residents (`Temporary residents (%)` registered with public security authorities as living >1 year away from their permanent address). As the authors acknowledge in their limitations (p. 790), the design tests city-level migrant demographic composition rather than a direct legal/administrative rule intervention.

2. Outcome / Criterion 4 (`borderline_institutional_or_compliance_outcome`): Among the five dependent variables in Table 3, three are non-WASH (`Public green space`, `Solid waste treatment capacity`, `Quantity of solid waste treated`) and two relate to municipal sewage/wastewater infrastructure (`Wastewater treatment capacity` in 10,000 m3/day per 10,000 persons and `Quantity of wastewater treated` in 10,000 m3/year per 10,000 persons). Neither wastewater metric measures household sanitation access, sewer connection, toilet coverage, water supply access, continuity, quality-as-access, or affordability. The authors explicitly note (p. 785) that limited information precludes ascertaining whether the local population directly benefits from pollutant treatment plant construction. Moreover, because total urban population (permanent + temporary) enters the denominator of both the predictor and the per-capita plant-capacity outcome, inflows of temporary migrants mechanically dilute per-capita municipal plant capacity unless plant expansion immediately keeps pace.

3. SWiM Family placement (`none_nonfit`): Although `hukou` non-recognition is thematically adjacent to Family A (legal status, tenure, recognition), pooling an ecological city-wide migrant-share regression on bulk municipal wastewater treatment plant capacity/throughput with household or settlement legal-recognition/tenure effects on household WASH service access would be construct-invalid. Note on sign/direction: the raw coefficients on `Temporary residents (%)` are negative (-0.00164 and -0.326), meaning a higher share of legally unrecognized temporary migrants is associated with lower per-capita municipal wastewater treatment capacity/volume (substantively, legal `hukou` exclusion harms infrastructure provision, or permanent legal recognition aligns positively with infrastructure supply).

raw_response.headline_estimate_summary: Two-way fixed-effects panel regressions (Table 3, PDF p. 9 / journal p. 788) testing the continuous exposure `Temporary residents (%)` (share of urban district population without permanent `hukou` registration; 1-percentage-point increase): (1) Model 2 — `Wastewater treatment capacity` (10,000 m3/day per 10,000 persons): beta = -0.00164, clustered SE = 0.000529, p < 0.01 (t = -3.10, approx. 95% CI [-0.00268, -0.00060]), equivalent to -16.4 m3/day per 10,000 persons per 1-percentage-point increase in temporary residents (N = 1,730 city-years, 283 cities, R2 = 0.065); (2) Model 3 — `Quantity of wastewater treated` (10,000 m3/year per 10,000 persons): beta = -0.326, clustered SE = 0.169, p < 0.10 (t = -1.93, approx. 95% CI [-0.657, +0.005]), equivalent to -3,260 m3/year per 10,000 persons (N = 1,737 city-years, 282 cities, R2 = 0.181). Non-WASH outcomes in Table 3: Public green space beta = 0.00594 (SE = 0.0212, NS, N = 1,769); Solid waste treatment capacity beta = -0.0897 (SE = 0.0268, p < 0.01, N = 1,577); Quantity of solid waste treated beta = -0.00136 (SE = 0.000732, p < 0.10, N = 1,589). All models adjust for logged population density, logged GRP per capita, high school/college enrollment (%), registered unemployment rate (%), logged municipal government spending per capita, city fixed effects, and year fixed effects, with city-clustered SEs. Raw negative sign means greater share without permanent `hukou` reduces per-capita wastewater infrastructure (substantively pro-recognition / harmful effect of legal exclusion).
raw_response.study_design_and_sample: Longitudinal two-way fixed-effects (city and year FE) panel regression study in urban China using prefecture-level city-year panel data from 2008 to 2014 (dataset covering 290 prefectural cities; analytic samples in Table 3: N = 1,730 city-years across 283 cities for wastewater treatment capacity; N = 1,737 city-years across 282 cities for quantity of wastewater treated; N = 1,769 across 283 cities for public green space; N = 1,577 and N = 1,589 across 276 cities for solid waste models).
